## What we measure and price

We measure and price single trade packages. Mostly for subcontractors bidding to a main contractor, sometimes for the main contractor checking what came back.

## How it works

::: {.process-steps}
::: {.process-step}
#### Send the pack
Drawings, the specification, the tender bill if there is one, and your return date.
:::

::: {.process-step}
#### We come back within one working day
You get the scope we would measure, a fixed fee and a delivery date.
:::

::: {.process-step}
#### You get the takeoff or priced bill
In your format, with the assumptions listed.
:::
:::

Priced per package, quoted before we start. No hourly billing and no fee for scope we did not agree.

## Who does the work

Robert Kowalski. Twenty years measuring and pricing construction work in the UK, Australia and Poland. Facade and cladding remediation, drylining and screed, firestopping, structural and masonry packages.

You deal with me directly. The person who measures your drawings is the person who answers the phone when your contracts manager queries a rate. I do not subcontract the measurement out, and I do not run more tenders at once than I can take proper care of. Where I use software to speed up measurement, I say so, and every quantity that leaves here has been checked against the drawings by hand.

::: {.split-panel}
::: {.two-col}
::: {.split-panel-text}
<h2>What to send us</h2>

<p>Drawings (PDF or DWG), the specification or NBS output, the tender bill if there is one, and your return date. IFC or Revit if you have a model. We do not need one.</p>

<p>If the pack is over 100 MB, email us and we send an upload link.</p>
:::

::: {.split-panel-text}
<h2>What happens next</h2>

<p>We read the pack and come back within one working day with the scope we would measure, a fixed fee and a delivery date.</p>

<p>If it is not a package we can do well, we say so and tell you who does.</p>

::: {.card-actions}

## Frequently asked questions

::: {.faq-section}
::: {.faq-item}
::: {.faq-question}
**Q: What do you need from me to start?**
:::
::: {.faq-answer}
A: Drawings as PDF or DWG, the specification or NBS output, the tender bill if there is one, and your return date. We read IFC from Revit, ArchiCAD and Tekla if you have a model, but we do not need one — most of what we measure comes off 2D drawings.
:::
:::

::: {.faq-item}
::: {.faq-question}
**Q: Is my package too small?**
:::
::: {.faq-answer}
A: No. Most of what we do is single trade packages.
:::
:::

::: {.faq-item}
::: {.faq-question}
**Q: What format does the takeoff or priced bill come back in?**
:::
::: {.faq-answer}
A: Yours. Excel in your estimating layout, a CITE/eBQ file for import, or the bill format your main contractor has issued. Tell us what your estimator works in and we deliver to it.
:::
:::

::: {.faq-item}
::: {.faq-question}
**Q: What does it cost?**
:::
::: {.faq-answer}
A: Priced per package, quoted before we start. No hourly billing and no fee for scope we did not agree.
:::
:::

::: {.faq-item}
::: {.faq-question}
**Q: How accurate are the quantities?**
:::
::: {.faq-answer}
A: Quantities are measured to the drawings and the specification you send. Where the information is incomplete we list the assumption rather than absorb it.
:::
:::
:::
